subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should native `openclaw backup create` add user-controlled exclude patterns now, and should that ship as only explicit `--exclude`/`--exclude-file` flags or also as smart defaults with protected-path guards?
rationale: This is a public backup CLI and recovery/security decision: excludes can prevent sensitive or huge files from entering archives, but defaults or weak guards can make backups incomplete or unrestorable.

options.title: Review a guarded native implementation
options.body: Keep this issue open and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288, or a narrower replacement, as the candidate once conflicts, proof, protected paths, and JSON/manifest compatibility are settled.

options.title: Ship minimal explicit excludes only
options.body: Limit the first core change to repeatable `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` without smart defaults, reducing product risk but leaving size guidance to users.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Document KeepMyClaw and existing broad backup flags as alternatives, accepting that native `openclaw backup create` still lacks fine-grained backup scope control.

recommendation.title: Review a guarded native implementation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288, or a narrower replacement, as the candidate once conflicts, proof, protected paths, and JSON/manifest compatibility are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup-path work plus broad product/security ownership signals make this the best available route for the policy choice.
